samples.text:
The pie chart shows the main causes of water pollution in a river basin in the year 2023.

As can be seen, agricultural run-off was the biggest source of the pollution with 37%. Urban sewage was the second one, it caused 26% of the pollution. Industrial discharge was also important and it was 18%.

The other sources was much smaller. Road drainage was 9% and mining was 6%. Other sources was the smallest part with just 4%. These three sources together was less than the urban sewage alone. Firstly, agricultural run-off was more than double of industrial discharge. Also, agriculture and sewage together was more than 60% of the total pollution, which is a very big part.

Overall, most of pollution in this river basin came from the agriculture, the cities and the industry. The three biggest sources together made 81% of pollution, and the three smallest sources only 19%. So farming was the most serious problem for the river in 2023.
samples.why: Accurate figures with relevant comparisons · overview placed late · linking is mechanical and sometimes misused (Firstly) · adequate vocabulary with repetition · several agreement and article errors that do not block meaning.

samples.text:
The pie chart illustrates the proportion of water pollution in a river basin that came from six different sources in 2023.

Overall, agricultural run-off was the single largest source of pollution, and together with urban sewage and industrial discharge it was responsible for the vast majority of the total. The remaining sources made a relatively minor contribution.

Agricultural run-off accounted for 37% of all pollution, which was more than a third of the total. Urban sewage was the second most significant source, contributing just over a quarter (26%), while industrial discharge made up 18%. Taken together, these three sources represented 81% of the pollution in the river basin.

By contrast, the other three sources were much less important. Road drainage was responsible for 9% of the pollution, which was half the figure for industrial discharge. Mining contributed 6%, and other sources accounted for only 4%, the smallest share. It is also worth noting that agricultural run-off alone produced almost twice as much pollution as road drainage, mining and other sources combined.
samples.why: Clear overview with appropriate grouping of sources · key features highlighted with accurate figures and correct comparisons · logical paragraphing · varied cohesive devices · good vocabulary · mostly error-free.

samples.text:
The chart breaks down the sources of water pollution in a river basin in 2023 into six categories.

The most notable feature is the dominance of agricultural run-off, which was the largest single contributor. More broadly, pollution was concentrated in three main sources, with agriculture, urban sewage and industry together accounting for roughly four-fifths of the total.

Agricultural run-off was responsible for 37% of the pollution, more than double the share attributable to industrial discharge (18%). Urban sewage ranked second at 26%, so agricultural and domestic sources combined generated almost two-thirds of all contamination entering the river system. Industrial discharge completed the three principal sources, bringing their joint share to 81%.

The three remaining sources were considerably less significant. Run-off from roads accounted for 9%, precisely half the industrial figure, while mining contributed 6% and miscellaneous sources a mere 4%. Collectively, these minor sources made up less than a fifth of the pollution, which is less than the contribution of urban sewage on its own. This distribution suggests that pollution in the basin stemmed overwhelmingly from a small number of large-scale sources rather than being evenly spread.
samples.why: Key features skilfully selected and grouped · well-placed overview · accurate figures and derived comparisons used purposefully · cohesion seamless · precise vocabulary (attributable, contamination) · wide range of error-free structures.
